summary: Remote-shell agent: WebSocket-driven PTY and loopback tunneling into the installer's host
details: The package runs as a CLI agent (`agentlink-client start`) that opens a persistent WebSocket to a configured relay server. On receiving `terminal_open` / `terminal_input` frames, `dist/terminal.js` spawns a PTY (`/bin/bash` on POSIX, `powershell.exe` on Windows) via `pty.spawn(shell, [],...)` and writes remote-supplied bytes directly into it — the relay peer obtains full-host interactive shell execution on the operator's machine. Separately, `dist/tunnel.js` handles `tunnel_request` / `tunnel_ws_open` / `tunnel_ws_message` frames by opening HTTP and WebSocket connections to `127.0.0.1:<port>` on the operator's host and relaying traffic back over the WebSocket, giving the relay operator a bridge into locally-bound services (the loopback tunnel is gated by an opt-in allowlist at `~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json`, disabled by default). The remote-shell channel itself is not gated by an allowlist and is the core advertised function of the tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
